doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Eddie Lang
summary: His impression of Eddie Lang as a complete soloist and the duets with Lonnie Johnson.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Let me run a few names by you and maybe they have an impression and maybe they don’t. Eddie Lang?
I don’t know his playing that well but I remember kind of like the father of modern kind of guitar. One of the fathers of modern guitar for sure but I remember his playing to be

very, I don’t know if virtuosic is the right word but he was more of a kind of almost like a soloist, like a real complete kind of guitarist. Could play chord melodies and kind of like a piano. He was more like a piano player when he played alone. I know that with the duets with Lonnie Johnson it was really interesting because you could hear these two really very different styles. Eddie sounded very, very calculated and in a way, very clean. And then of course Lonnie was more of a blues player. So I thought it was interesting that they were a team that played together.
